clue.text: Looks back, facing Sodom initially

parts.note: to countenance something is to back it or give it approval

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word Sodom

explanation.surface: Someone glances backwards towards Sodom at the start, like Lot's wife about to turn to salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads as a direction but is a verb meaning support; 'facing' merely joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Faces or expressions are what a person's looks show, a standard synonym for the plural noun.

clue.text: Cover can include Independent leader

parts.note: a cap is a covering, as for a head or bottle

indicators.note: include means the can holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
no word in the clue gives this letter; the setter admitted on the blog that the clue omits it

explanation.surface: A lid can hold in an Independent party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue is flawed: no word gives the A. On the blog the setter admitted 'I saw what I wanted to see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the person in command of a team or ship, its leader.

clue.text: Headless lack of purpose provides the opposite

indicators.note: headless says the opening letter is cut off the word for lack of purpose

parts.note: futility is pointlessness, a lack of purpose

explanation.surface: Something without direction or aim turns out to be surprisingly useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the clue: the opposite of futility (pointlessness) is usefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Usefulness is the contrary of pointlessness, so 'the opposite' of futility names it.

clue.text: Time slowed down taking second to change

indicators.note: taking means the phrase for slowed down takes another piece inside it

parts.note: a train that is delayed has run behind schedule: it ran late

explanation.surface: A clock ran slow and needed a second's adjustment to set it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slowed down' reads as one verb but is the phrase 'ran late', as a delayed train did.
explanation.definitionFit: To render words in another language is to convert or alter them, so change works as a looser synonym.

clue.text: Creature seen in many a lake

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are visible inside the words many a lake

explanation.surface: Wildlife spotted at many a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is an antelope, so it is an example of a creature.

clue.text: Part of body almost swelled getting gangrene

definitions.note: used as a verb: to become gangrenous

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the body part

parts.note: the neck is a part of the body
rose means swelled, as a river or dough does

explanation.surface: A wound on the body has swollen and is turning gangrenous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gangrene' is a verb here, meaning to go gangrenous; 'getting' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue that necroses dies off, which is what flesh does when it turns gangrenous.

clue.text: Fellow feeling compiler up and slap hardly ends!

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word for the compiler is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the compiler, the setter, refers to themself as me
a pat is a light slap

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of the word hardly

explanation.surface: The setter, outraged, exclaims at a mere tap of a slap being called sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler' is the setter, ME, which 'up' turns to EM in this down entry; 'ends' of hardly give HY.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the sharing of another person's emotions, which is fellow feeling.

clue.text: Persuading supporter where Obama lives to lose weight

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: to lose says a piece is taken out of the place phrase

parts.note: Obama, then US president, lived in Washington
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A political backer from Obama's home town is urged to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where Obama lives' is IN WASHINGTON; 'to lose' removes TON, leaving IN WASHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainwashing is forcing someone into new beliefs, an extreme form of persuasion.

clue.text: Queen record with guitar flourish … cut a copy

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: cut trims the last letter from the guitar flourish

parts.note: a lick is a short showy phrase on the guitar

explanation.surface: The band Queen release a record with a guitar solo trimmed, a tribute version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the rock band but is R (Regina); 'cut' removes the K of LICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an object, i.e. a copy.

clue.text: Police work chasing mobster's booze

indicators.note: chasing means the police and work pieces come after the mobster

parts.note: Al Capone was the archetypal mobster
a cop is a police officer
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Police pursue a gangster's illicit liquor, Prohibition-style.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is Al Capone, Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet fruit-flavoured alcoholic drink, a kind of booze.

clue.text: Demonstrate embodying New Age apprehension

indicators.note: embodying means the word for demonstrate holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to present something is to show or demonstrate it
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A New Age protest stirs up anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' looks like one phrase but splits in two: N for new, and age as a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a feeling that something bad will happen, i.e. a sense of apprehension.

clue.text: Characters having inclination towards the right

definitions.text: Characters having inclination towards the right

parts.words: Characters having inclination towards the right
parts.note: reads as people with right-wing leanings, but means printed letters that slope rightwards

explanation.surface: People who lean to the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type is lettering that slants to the right, so italic characters lean that way.

clue.text: Missionary position being embraced by topless man

indicators.note: being embraced by means the position is held inside the other piece
topless takes the first letter off the word for man

parts.note: a man is a male
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A saucy picture: the missionary position and a topless man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missionary position' looks like one phrase but 'Missionary' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the first Christian missionaries, and the word still names a pioneering missionary.

clue.text: Masculine women supplanting male in a feeble way

indicators.note: supplanting says one letter takes the place of another in the word for masculine

parts.note: manly means masculine

explanation.surface: Butch women displace a man, rather weakly.
explanation.walkthrough: W (women) replaces the M (male) at the start of MANLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanly means palely and weakly, so it describes doing something in a feeble way.

clue.text: Model bent endlessly, totally gutted by exercise

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the word for bent

parts.note: arched means bent into a curve

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of totally, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A fashion model, bent over and completely exhausted from a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like 'devastated' but strips TOTALLY to its outer letters TY.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is an original pattern from which copies derive, a prototype or model.

clue.text: Oddly, chap to head riskiest release

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and further odd-numbered letters of chap to head riskiest

explanation.surface: A strange fellow heads for the most dangerous thrill to let off steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the purging of pent-up emotion, an emotional release.

clue.text: Shortest dance embracing maiden that's missing date

indicators.note: embracing means the word for dance holds the maiden inside

parts.note: to skip is to dance or caper
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: missing removes the date letter from the Latin phrase

parts.note: id est, Latin for that is, gives the abbreviation i.e.

explanation.surface: The briefest of dances around a young woman who has missed her date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is ID EST (that is); 'missing' takes out D, leaving IEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpiest describes the scantiest or most meagre, as of clothing, so the shortest.

clue.text: Musical virtually without backing raised from state

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means the whole is read from bottom to top
without here means outside, so the musical goes round the backing
virtually means almost all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Annie is a stage musical
aid is help or backing

explanation.surface: A show nearly lost its funding when it moved out of a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: ANNI goes round AID to give ANAIDNI, which 'raised' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Imagine Scot pickled with no limits

parts.note: the Picts were ancient inhabitants of Scotland

indicators.note: with no limits strips the first and last letters off the word for pickled

parts.note: cured means preserved, as by pickling

explanation.surface: Picture a Scotsman completely drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' suggests drunk but means CURED, which loses its ends to give URE.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, i.e. to imagine it.

clue.text: Sectarian shot in scrap

indicators.note: in places the shot inside the scrap

parts.note: a bit is a scrap or small piece
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A sectarian is shot in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight but is BIT, a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sectarian holds narrow, intolerant views of other groups, the mark of a bigot.

clue.text: Pitt's the greatest, we hear, boring tool!

parts.note: the actor Brad Pitt, not the Prime Minister

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: all is the most there is, the greatest amount

explanation.surface: A fan insists Pitt is the best, though the films he's in are tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitt' suggests the Georgian prime ministers but is the film star Brad Pitt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small pointed hand tool used for boring holes in wood.

clue.text: Choke from carburettor a garage put back

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A car's choke is removed from the carburettor and returned to the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: To garotte is to strangle, which is to choke someone.

clue.text: Tempts Italian leader into immorality, first to last

indicators.note: into puts the leader inside the rearranged word for immorality
first to last moves the opening letter of the word for immorality to its end

parts.note: sin is immorality
Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Italian leader

explanation.surface: Mussolini lures someone into depravity.
explanation.walkthrough: Il Duce was Mussolini's title; 'first to last' moves the opening letter of the word for immorality to its end before the leader goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade or lure them into acting, i.e. to tempt.

clue.text: Cricket ground since over without a volley

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the pieces are turned upside down
without says the letter a is taken out of the cricket ground

parts.note: The Oval is a London cricket ground
as means since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: At a cricket ground, a bowler's over passes without a volley being hit.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; losing an A gives OVL, plus AS, and 'over' flips the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, i.e. a volley.

clue.text: Sheet is one of these

parts.note: the word sheet is a rearrangement of the letters of the word these in the clue

explanation.surface: A sheet belongs to some category of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet and these share the same letters, so each is a jumble of the other.

clue.text: Even admire fabulous ship nearly capsizing

indicators.note: capsizing turns everything over, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to laud is to praise or admire

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter of the ship's name

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Steady admiration for a legendary vessel about to overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means of fable: ARGO, Jason's ship, less its O; 'capsizing' reverses LAUD + ARG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual slope is even and steady rather than steep or abrupt.

clue.text: Severe scrap in 'correctional' institution

indicators.note: in places the scrap inside the institution

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is where ill health is corrected
a part is a scrap or fragment

explanation.surface: A harsh fight in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes warn that the 'correctional' place is a sanatorium (SAN), not a prison; 'scrap' is PART, not a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and harsh, as life in ancient Sparta was, hence severe.

clue.text: Passionate European one in French department?

definitions.text: Passionate European one in French department?

parts.note: mad means passionate, as in mad about someone

indicators.note: in places the one inside the French department

parts.note: Moselle is a département in eastern France
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fiery young European woman living in a French province.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a young French woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for an unmarried young woman, one found in France.
